title: Test status and side effects together

Walk through: A function can append an event and then return rejected. Checking only the string would miss the violation. Ask: Which assertion detects that bug? Expected answer and boundary: Assert that the event count and protected state are unchanged for every rejected action. Visual purpose: show Returned status | Action log | State mutation. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. title: Simulated timeout is not process isolation
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Simulated timeout is not process isolation. Define: A fake slow-step flag exercises an error branch, not operating-system enforcement. Walk through: The notebook has no blocking network tool. A production tool requires real timeout and cancellation controls. Ask: Why avoid claiming runtime security here? Expected answer and boundary: An in-process check cannot forcibly stop arbitrary blocking code. The demonstration only tests control-flow handling. Visual purpose: show Simulated timeout | Real wall clock | Worker isolation. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. [Sources] https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents ; https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1. Original teaching example, not an empirical deployment claim. title: Retry only a declared transient failure
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Retry only a declared transient failure. Define: A bounded retry preserves the original request and logs each attempt. Walk through: Timeout may be retryable for a read; permission_denied is never repaired by repeated calls. Ask: What if a request has a side effect? Expected answer and boundary: A retry can duplicate it. Use idempotency keys or transactional semantics, not blind re-execution. Visual purpose: show Transient error > Remaining budget? > Retry once > Stop. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation.
